intro: The Azores' great trees are imports that found a home: Moreton Bay Figs from Australia and Norfolk Island Pines from the Pacific, planted in the gardens of nineteenth-century São Miguel. In Ponta Delgada the Jardim António Borges keeps a fig the regional government calls colossal, and another fig by the Jardim José do Canto came second in Portugal's Tree of the Year 2026. In Furnas, Parque Terra Nostra's Lady of the Park is about 200 years old by the park's own figure.
meta_description: The Azores' remarkable trees on São Miguel: Ponta Delgada's giant figs and Terra Nostra's Lady of the Park, where each stands and how to visit.
question_meta: São Miguel's best-known trees are Ponta Delgada's Moreton Bay Figs and the Norfolk Island Pine of Terra Nostra in Furnas.
question_answer: The remarkable trees of the Azores are on São Miguel. In Ponta Delgada, the Jardim António Borges has a Moreton Bay Fig the regional government calls colossal, and a Moreton Bay Fig by the Jardim José do Canto came second in Portugal's Tree of the Year 2026. In Furnas, about 45 minutes away, Parque Terra Nostra's Norfolk Island Pine, the Lady of the Park, is about 200 years old by the park's own figure.
question_context: Locally both figs are called Australian rubber trees; botanists know them as Moreton Bay Figs, Ficus macrophylla. The Jardim António Borges was laid out between 1858 and 1861 and belongs to Ponta Delgada's council, and entry is free, but no source dates its fig to the first planting, so its age stays open. The Tree of the Year runner-up drew on more than 18,000 votes nationally; two more Moreton Bay Figs grow inside the José do Canto garden, and nothing on record ties the entry to one trunk, so the pin follows the tree mapped under the contest's name. Terra Nostra's figures of 52 metres and about 200 years are the park's own, published for the same contest, and the pin is the araucaria mapped as A Araucária do Terra Nostra among a ring of them by the thermal pool. The Azores created a regional register of classified trees in 2026, which may settle some of these questions once its list is published.

faq.q: Which Azores tree was in Portugal's Tree of the Year?
faq.a: Two were entered in 2026. The Australian rubber tree of Ponta Delgada, a Moreton Bay Fig by the Jardim José do Canto, finished second behind the cedar of Runa. Parque Terra Nostra also entered its Norfolk Island Pine, the Lady of the Park.

faq.q: Is the Jardim António Borges free?
faq.a: Yes, it is a municipal garden owned by Ponta Delgada's council, about ten minutes on foot from the Portas da Cidade.

trees.name: Giant Australian Rubber Tree of Jardim Antonio Borges

location.address: Jardim Antonio Borges, Rua Antonio Borges, Ponta Delgada, Sao Miguel

trees.access: Free public access, municipal garden (owned by Ponta Delgada council since 1957); opening hours not published on the sources read
trees.transport: Central Ponta Delgada, about 10 minutes on foot from the Portas da Cidade / Campo de Sao Francisco
trees.verify_notes: SIARAM (Direcao Regional do Ambiente, Azores) garden sheet updated Dec 2014 calls it the colossal Australian fig (Ficus macrophylla) with fantastic aerial roots, in the south-east sector of the garden, among the largest and oldest specimens of the botanical route along the Central Alley, labelled with botanical identification. OSM natural=tree node 3761891663 named Ficus Macrophylla stands inside the garden (way relation 12768197), consistent with the south-east sector; pin from the OSM tree node, SIARAM gives no coordinate. Alive: iNaturalist observation 2026-10-09 (https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/406984254) via lifecheck.py RECENT. Age: no source gives one; garden built 1858 to 1861 (planting plans from 1861-69) but no source ties this fig to that planting, so no age (no bridge). No girth or height found. Other notables there per same SIARAM sheet: Araucaria columnaris by the tea house, Araucaria bidwillii, big jacaranda, cork oak over the royal coach, Podocarpus, Norfolk pine near small lake, Picconia azorica. Flagged: one regional source plus OSM; no measurement.
trees.story:
In the Azores this is an Australian rubber tree. Botanists know it as a Moreton Bay Fig, and the regional government's own sheet on the Jardim António Borges simply calls it colossal. That sheet, from the Azorean environment directorate, singles it out for its fantastic aerial roots and counts it among the largest and oldest trees on the garden's botanical route.

The fig grows in the south-east part of the garden, along the Central Alley, and carries a botanical label, so it is not hard to find. Its roots are the point. A Moreton Bay Fig lets them down from its branches. Nobody has published its girth or height, so the word colossal is the only measurement on record.

The garden around it was laid out between 1858 and 1861, with planting plans running through the 1860s, and it has belonged to Ponta Delgada's council since 1957. That makes it tempting to date the fig to the first planting. No source we have found does, so its age stays open. If you know when it went in, tell us.

It is good company. The same sheet names a Cook Pine by the tea house, a Bunya Pine, a large jacaranda and a cork oak sheltering an old royal coach. Entry is free, and the garden is about ten minutes on foot from the Portas da Cidade in the centre of Ponta Delgada.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the mass of aerial roots and its botanical label. It stands in the south-east part of the garden, along the Central Alley.

trees.name: Australian Rubber Tree of Ponta Delgada

location.address: Rua Calco da Ma Cara, beside Jardim Jose do Canto, Ponta Delgada, Sao Miguel

trees.access: Tree stands at the street edge on Rua Calco da Ma Cara next to the Jose do Canto garden; the street side is public, garden entry is separate and not checked
trees.transport: Central Ponta Delgada, about 10 minutes on foot from Campo de Sao Francisco
trees.verify_notes: DN (fetched) reports the Arvore-de-Borracha-Australiana in Ponta Delgada, Acores, took second place on the national Tree of the Year 2026 podium behind the Runa cedar, of 18,000+ votes overall; no figure or age for this tree on the DN page. A search summary (Portugal News, 2026-04-16, page itself would not fetch, so NOT a source) says it was planted 1870 by Jose do Canto; unverified, so no age recorded. Pin: OSM natural=tree node 13359031098 carries the exact contest name 'Arvore-da-Borracha-Australiana' on Rua Calco da Ma Cara by the Jose do Canto garden wall; not matched to the contest entry by a source, so kept approximate. Alive: iNaturalist 2025-06-29 (https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/295055534) via lifecheck RECENT. A second Ficus macrophylla node (OSM 12020707815 and 12020707823) stands inside Jardim Jose do Canto at 37.74926,-25.67029 and 37.74789,-25.67068; whether any of them is the contest tree needs the candidacy page (arvoredoanoportugal) or the city council. Flagged: contest tree identity unconfirmed.
trees.story:
In 2026 Portugal voted this fig the second best tree in the country. The national Tree of the Year contest drew more than 18,000 votes, the Diário de Notícias reported, and the Australian rubber tree of Ponta Delgada finished on the podium behind the cedar of Runa in Torres Vedras. Australian rubber tree is the local name for a Moreton Bay Fig.

There is one honest complication. Two more Moreton Bay Figs are mapped inside the Jardim José do Canto, just behind it. The tree on this pin is the one mapped under the contest's exact name, at the street edge of Rua Calço da Má Cara against the garden wall, but nothing on record ties the entry to this trunk. If you voted for it, or know which tree it was, tell us.

No published figure gives its age, girth or height, so the contest result is the strongest thing on record for it. For a tree native to the far side of the world, second place in a country of cork oaks and olives is a fair result.

The street side is public and needs no ticket. The garden behind the wall has its own entrance. It is about ten minutes on foot from the Campo de São Francisco in central Ponta Delgada.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its place at the street edge of Rua Calço da Má Cara, against the wall of the José do Canto garden. Two more Moreton Bay Figs stand inside the garden.

trees.name: Lady of the Park, Terra Nostra Norfolk Pine

location.address: Parque Terra Nostra, Rua do Parque, Furnas, Povoacao, Sao Miguel

trees.access: Paid entry to Parque Terra Nostra (Bensaude Hotels); fee and hours on the park ticket page, not read
trees.transport: Furnas village, park is on Rua do Parque in the village; Furnas is about 45 minutes by car from Ponta Delgada, no practical public bus for a day trip checked
trees.verify_notes: Owner (Parque Terra Nostra news page, fetched) nominated it for Tree of the Year 2026 as the Lady of the Park, a Norfolk Island pine of about 200 years and 52 m high, in the heart of Furnas valley, no spot given in the park. 52 m is the owner's claim and high for a Norfolk pine in the Azores; record as claimed, do not sharpen. OSM node 13359031096 named 'A Araucaria do Terra Nostra' at 37.77128,-25.31475 is the only mapped candidate; the park has a ring of araucarias round the thermal pool and the node is not tied to this one by a source, so approximate. Alive: iNaturalist 2026-07-27 (https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/385641636) via lifecheck RECENT. Park founded 1780s by Thomas Hickling, enlarged 1935; the national result for the entry was not found. Flagged: owner source only, location in the park unconfirmed.
trees.story:
Parque Terra Nostra calls this tree the Lady of the Park and says she is 52 metres tall. That is the park's own figure, published when it entered her for Portugal's Tree of the Year 2026, and it is a remarkable one for a Norfolk Island Pine on the Azores. Nobody independent has measured her, so read it as a claim, not a record.

The park also puts her age at about 200 years, and that is the only estimate there is. Terra Nostra goes back to the 1780s, when Thomas Hickling founded a garden in the Furnas valley, and it was enlarged in 1935. No source connects the Lady to either moment, so her age stays the park's word.

Which araucaria is she? A ring of them stands around the park's thermal pool, and the nomination did not say where she grows. The pin is the single tree mapped under the name A Araucária do Terra Nostra, the best candidate but not a certainty. If you have stood under her and know which one it is, tell us.

She stands in the heart of the Furnas valley, in the park's words, and the park is a paid garden in the village itself, about 45 minutes by car from Ponta Delgada. The result of her national entry is not on record yet.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the name it is mapped under, A Araucária do Terra Nostra. It stands among the ring of araucarias around the park's thermal pool.

trees.name: Pohutukawa of Campo de São Francisco

location.address: Campo de São Francisco (Praça 5 de Outubro), Ponta Delgada, São Miguel

official_register.name: Património Classificado dos Açores: Exemplares Arbóreos (SMG_IIM_36), Governo dos Açores

trees.access: Free. Public square in the centre of Ponta Delgada, open at all hours (no gate found). Branches are held by steel props and cables; the tree is viewed from around it.
trees.transport: Central Ponta Delgada, walkable from the old town; bus stops not checked.
trees.verify_notes: ONE OF TWO register-backed Azores icons. Register SMG_IIM_36 (Interesse Municipal under the 2015 decree; act: Diario do Governo II serie n.126, 28 May 1965, the first tree classified in the Azores per the Terra Livre / Em Defesa das Plantas blogs; the 2013 Lusa piece in Acoriano Oriental calls it classified of public interest, so the register level and the press disagree, use the register). Register species is written Metrosiderus tomentosa A. Cunn., OSM carries the same spelling; the Wikidata item, the blog and komoot say Metrosideros excelsa (pohutukawa, New Zealand Christmas tree). Kept excelsa (Wikidata label, blog by a local botanist); the register name is an older spelling/misidentification, noted. Pin: OSM node 3106113528 (natural=tree, historic=tree, name Metrosidero, wikidata Q66815855, last edited 2025-09-22) 11 m from the register point 37.737718,-25.672869 (register note: validated 29/11/2021 by orthophoto 2017/18). iNaturalist Metrosideros excelsa observations 2026-07-20 (accuracy 3 m, id 385264767) and 2026-09-26 (id 403504844) at the same spot = alive now. Lifecheck RECENT 2026-09-26. Size: OSM tags circumference 5 m, height 12, crown diameter 23 m (unsourced contributor tags, girth_cm 500 recorded with that caveat); a Tripadvisor summary seen only as a search snippet claimed 7.6 m girth and 18 m, never fetched, not used. The species 'on average' reaches 20 m and crowns over 30 m (blog) but this specimen's height is not documented. Age: blog says planted about 1870 so about 150 years; the Terra Livre 2016 post says about 125 years; also listed by A. Emiliano Costa in 1953 as a notable tree (Boletim da Comissao Reguladora dos Cereais, n.17). No documented planting record for this specimen; page should stay vague. History: 2013 municipal intervention by Planeta das Arvores (study by arborist Serafim Riem) to prolong its life: rebalancing pruning, crown reduction, more reinforcing cables between branches and more vertical props (Lusa, 29 Jul 2013). Flowers red in May to July (blog). Who introduced it is unknown (a columnist guesses Antonio Borges, no source). Dedicated Wikidata/Commons category exists: 'Metrosidero on Praca 5 de Outubro (Ponta Delgada)'. Photo approved 2026-11-02 after looking at the pixels: tree fills the frame, daylight, survives the card crop.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the one huge, many-stemmed crown that fills the square, held up by steel props and cables, red with flowers from May to July. It stands beside the bandstand.
trees.story:
By the count of two Azorean plant blogs, this was the first tree the islands ever protected, classified in May 1965. It is a pohutukawa, the New Zealand Christmas tree, and it has spent well over a century spreading across the Campo de São Francisco in the middle of Ponta Delgada.

The crown is the reason to come. Volunteer mappers give it a spread of 23 metres and a trunk about five metres round. Nobody official has published those numbers, so treat them as rough. What anyone can see is the engineering. In 2013 the council brought in arborists to prolong its life. They rebalanced and reduced the crown, added cables between the limbs and set more steel props beneath them. The tree now leans on its crutches beside the bandstand.

Its age rests on two local estimates. A botanist's blog says it went in around 1870, which makes it about 150; a post from 2016 put it at about 125. No planting record survives. It was already on a list of the island's notable trees in 1953.

Even its name is disputed. The regional register writes Metrosideros tomentosa, an older name; Wikidata and the local botanist say Metrosideros excelsa. The register also files it as of municipal interest, where the press has called it of public interest.

Come between May and July, when the crown flowers red. The square is public and open at all hours.

best_time.label: May to July, when the whole crown flowers red

trees.name: Giant Norfolk Island Pine of Lagoa das Furnas

location.address: Margem sul da Lagoa das Furnas, beside the Centro de Monitorização e Investigação das Furnas, Furnas, Povoação, São Miguel

official_register.name: Património Classificado dos Açores: Exemplares Arbóreos (SMG_IIP_66, Interesse Público, Resolução do Conselho do Governo n.º 13/2011 of 2 Feb 2011), Governo dos Açores

trees.access: Free. Stands on the lakeshore on public regional-government ground (register owner 'Público/RAA', land of SPRAçores), beside the flat dirt lakeside trail (PRC06SMI circular walk) near the Furnas environmental interpretation centre (OSM: museum, Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00). An information board stands next to the tree (OSM node 13027000663).
trees.transport: Furnas, about 40 km east of Ponta Delgada by road; reached on foot along the signed PRC06SMI lake walk (9.4 km loop from Furnas village) or by car to the lakeshore parking at the interpretation centre. Bus links not checked.
trees.verify_notes: Register SMG_IIP_66, classified of public interest by Resolucao do Conselho do Governo 13/2011 (press reports it in Jan 2011). Two independent press sources agree on height: Lusa/DN 16 Jan 2010 quotes SPRAcores administrator Helia Palha: found during clearing of an old wood on the south shore, species Araucaria heterophylla, 'between 150 and 200 years', 50.10 m tall and 1.90 m in DIAMETER; Acoriano Oriental 13 Jan 2011: about 50 m tall, trunk 'diameter' of nearly six metres. The two diameters conflict; 1.90 m x pi = 5.97 m, so the 'six metres' is almost certainly the circumference (girth_cm 597 derived from the 1.90 m diameter; OSM tags circumference 1.9 m, which confuses the two). Age is the SPRAcores estimate at discovery in 2010, so 16 years added to 150-200 gives 166-216 (rounded). Press and the official trail page call it the largest classified Norfolk pine in Europe / among the largest in the world: attribute, not verified; the OSM board text says 'One of the world's largest Norfolk Island Pines'. OSM height tag 50 matches. Pin: OSM node 10106097684 (natural=tree, species Araucaria heterophylla, last edit 2026-10-08), 20 m from register point 37.750977,-25.338702. iNaturalist: Araucaria heterophylla observations 2026-07-15 (accuracy 7 m, id 381706378), 2026-07-03, 2025-08-02 (accuracy 14 m) all within about 25 m = alive, GPS-supported. Lifecheck RECENT 2026-07-15. Discovery story: found 'by chance' in January 2010 during requalification work on the lake margins, 'which drew attention by its size'; protection means a 50 m protection radius and no felling or pruning without authorisation (Acoriano Oriental). Official trail page (Governo dos Acores, visitazores) places 'the largest classified araucaria in Europe' on the PRC06SMI route after the interpretation centre.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, a tiered conifer of about 50 metres rising above everything on the lakeshore, with an information board beside it. It stands on the lake walk near the Furnas interpretation centre.
trees.story:
A tree fifty metres tall stood on the shore of Lagoa das Furnas, and nobody had noticed it until January 2010. Workers clearing an old wood along the south margin of the lake came across it by chance, and it caught their attention by its size. SPRAçores, the regional company that manages the land, put it at 50.10 metres with a trunk 1.90 metres across.

That diameter means a trunk about six metres round, and a year later a newspaper reported nearly six metres, but called it the diameter. SPRAçores also estimated its age at discovery at between 150 and 200 years, so somewhere around 165 to 215 today. No planting record exists.

It is a Norfolk Island Pine, from a small island in the Pacific, and within a year of being found the Azores classified it of public interest. That gave it a 50-metre protection radius, and nobody may fell or prune it without permission.

The press and the regional government's trail page call it the largest classified araucaria in Europe, and the board beside it says one of the largest Norfolk Island Pines in the world. Neither claim comes with a comparison we could check. In Furnas village, Parque Terra Nostra says its own Norfolk pine reaches 52 metres, by the park's figure.

It is free to see. The signed PRC06SMI walk, a 9.4 km loop from Furnas village, passes it after the interpretation centre, where there is lakeshore parking.

trees.name: Coast Redwood of Mata-Jardim José do Canto

location.address: Mata-Jardim José do Canto, Caminho da Margem Sul da Lagoa das Furnas, 9675-040 Furnas, Povoação, São Miguel (register site name: Lugar do Torninho)

official_register.name: Património Classificado dos Açores: Exemplares Arbóreos (SMG_IIM_34, Interesse Municipal, despacho of 14 Oct 1970), Governo dos Açores

trees.access: Paid entry, inside the private botanical garden Mata-Jardim José do Canto (open to the public since 2014): EUR 5 per person from age 13, under 13 free. April to September 10:00-18:00 daily; October to March 09:00-17:00, Tuesday to Sunday (closed Mondays in winter). Last admission 30 minutes before closing (official site, read 2026-11-02).
trees.transport: Garden entrance on the south shore of Lagoa das Furnas, about 40 km (about 40 minutes by car) from Ponta Delgada per the garden's own page; bus links not checked.
trees.verify_notes: FLAGGED: single register plus map evidence, no measurement. Register SMG_IIM_34 'Sequoia ... Lugar do Torninho, Furnas' (despacho 14 Oct 1970; register note: location supplied by the Terceira environment service). The register gives no girth, height or age. That this tree stands INSIDE Mata-Jardim Jose do Canto is established only indirectly: the Commons category named after the register item (Wikidata Q66815867, 'Lugar do Torninho') holds CC0 photographs by Jan Helebrant whose file description says 'Mata Jardim Jose do Canto botanic garden', geotagged 70-100 m from the pin; the garden's own page (Futurismo/Visit Ponta Delgada text) and a travel blog mention towering/huge sequoias in the garden. Not a fact that the garden's marketing names THIS tree. Pin: OSM node 6550437710 (natural=tree, genus Sequoia, wikidata Q66815867, last edit 2026-04-21) sits 98 m from the register point 37.742861,-25.333321; its coordinates equal the Wikidata P625 to 7 decimals, so it may be copied from Wikidata rather than surveyed; iNaturalist Sequoia sempervirens observations of 2023-06-22 (id 168811343, 37.742597,-25.334294, 8 m from the node, no accuracy given) and 2023-07-17 (id 194535851, accuracy 113 m) support the spot. Called confirmed on the OSM-node criterion; downgrade to approximate if that is judged copied. Alive: lifecheck RECENT 2026-08-20 (iNat id 393295213). A 1953 text (A. Emiliano Costa, Boletim da Comissao Reguladora dos Cereais n.17, quoted in the Terra Livre blog) gives a sequoia of 4.27 m perimeter at breast height in the Mata-Jardim Jose do Canto on the lake margin; NOT recorded as this tree's girth because the text does not say it is the classified one. Age: garden laid out 1845-1885 by José do Canto but no source dates this specimen; left empty (no bridge claim). Winter hours conflict: a search summary said open daily, the garden's own visit and contact pages both say Tuesday to Sunday in winter; used the pages. Photo held: a person poses at the trunk and nothing ties the file to the register trunk (2026-11-02).
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the redwood standing above the garden's other trees. It stands inside the ticketed Mata-Jardim José do Canto on the lake's south shore, near the start of the garden's Salto do Rosal waterfall trail.
trees.story:
In October 1970 a redwood on the south shore of Lagoa das Furnas was classified of municipal interest, and the register has said almost nothing about it since. No girth, no height, no age. Just the genus and a place name, Lugar do Torninho.

That place, as far as the evidence goes, lies inside the Mata-Jardim José do Canto, a botanical garden that José do Canto laid out between 1845 and 1885 and that has been open to the public since 2014. The link is indirect. Photographs filed under the register entry describe the garden, the tree is mapped within it, and nature-app sightings of a coast redwood agree with the spot. The garden's own pages mention towering sequoias, plural, without naming this one.

A survey of the island's notable trees from 1953 recorded a sequoia 4.27 metres round at chest height in this garden by the lake. The text does not say it is the tree classified seventeen years later, so that number stays with the survey and off this trunk.

Nor has anyone dated it. The garden goes back to 1845, but no source says when this redwood went in. If you know, tell us.

Entry is paid, 5 euros from age 13 and free below. From April to September the garden opens daily from 10:00 to 18:00; from October to March, 09:00 to 17:00 and closed on Mondays. It is about 40 minutes by car from Ponta Delgada.

trees.name: Norfolk Island Pine of Jardim António Borges

location.address: Jardim António Borges, Rua António Borges, Ponta Delgada, São Miguel (near the small lake)
location.neighbourhood: Bairro da Vitória, São José, Ponta Delgada

trees.access: Free. Municipal garden of Ponta Delgada, public and free since 1957 (SIARAM). OSM opening_hours tag (sourced to the council page, not re-read): June to October Mon-Fri 09:00-20:00, Sat-Sun 09:00-21:00; November to May daily 09:00-18:00.
trees.transport: Inside Ponta Delgada, about 130 m from the garden's famous rubber tree (azo_001); bus stops not checked.
trees.verify_notes: FLAGGED: ground-owner source only, no measurement. SIARAM (Governo dos Acores, garden description) lists the 'majestosa Araucaria-de-Norfolk (Araucaria heterophylla) nas imediacoes do lago pequeno' among the largest and oldest specimens of the garden's botanical route, in the northern sector; the same text names the colossal Australian fig (live azo_001), a columnar araucaria by the Tea House (Araucaria columnaris) and a Bunya (A. bidwillii), so a visitor must tell the Norfolk pine apart from these. Not a registered tree. Pin: OSM node 12025325543 (natural=tree, name Norfolk Island Pine, 2024-07-01, version 1) inside the garden relation 12768197, beside the Grotto node; iNaturalist Araucaria genus observation 2026-07-08 (id 381252759, accuracy 5 m) lies 7 m from the node and an A. heterophylla observation 2026-06-05 (id 369308413) about 30 m: the node and iNat agree, but the node is a single volunteer's mapping. No height, girth or age in any source seen. Alive: lifecheck RECENT 2026-09-28. The page should say that the garden holds several araucaria species. Because the supporting evidence is thin, expect a short entry; the tree is worth a place only as the tallest conifer of a garden already on the map.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the tall tiered conifer near the small lake in the northern half of the garden. The columnar araucaria by the Tea House and the Bunya Pine below it are different species.
trees.story:
The Jardim António Borges grows at least three kinds of araucaria, and only one of them comes from Norfolk Island. The regional government's description of the garden singles this one out and counts it among the largest and oldest trees on the garden's botanical route. It stands near the small lake, in the northern half of the garden.

The other two are worth knowing, because they are what you will mistake it for. A columnar araucaria, Araucaria columnaris, grows by the Tea House, and a Bunya Pine stands below it. The Norfolk Island Pine is the tall tiered conifer by the small lake.

That government description is nearly all there is. The tree is not on the Azores' register of classified trees, nobody has published its height or girth, and the pin comes from a single volunteer's map, which nature-app sightings of araucarias a few metres away support. The garden was laid out between 1858 and 1861 and has been public and free since 1957, but no source says this pine went in with the first planting, so its age stays open. If you know it, tell us.

What it does have is company. About 130 metres away grows the garden's colossal Moreton Bay Fig, the tree most visitors come for, so one walk takes in both. The garden is in central Ponta Delgada. From June to October it opens 09:00 to 20:00 on weekdays and to 21:00 at weekends; from November to May, 09:00 to 18:00 daily.
